members.name: held
members.note:
This is not the recommended way to read rows: it holds the connection while your code runs for each row.
The reader, and the connection under it, stay open for as long as your code takes per row, added up over all the rows.
In async code that time has no bound: every in the loop body can yield, and nothing says when the loop resumes. Until it does, the connection is on hold: a pooled connection is not returned to the pool, and the server may keep its locks and the open result set.
These members suit work that must happen while the connection is open, for example a result too large to buffer or a row-by-row pipeline. Otherwise use a call that lets go of the connection first:
and
buffer the rows and release the connection (call .Map<T>() first), and
streams them to a consumer without holding it (the producer is unbounded: it reads without waiting for the consumer and frees the connection while the consumer takes its time, and the rows wait in memory until the consumer takes them; dispose the enumerator, as does).

members.name: held-reader
members.para: The same holds when you pass in a reader you opened yourself: the connection under it is held.

members.name: connection
members.para: The connection is opened if it is closed, and closed again when the call finishes; a connection that was already open is left as it was. A connection this call opened is also closed, never disposed, when the reader cannot be created.

members.name: row-pool
members.para: When is not , each row array is rented from it, can be longer than the number of values, and is yielded to the caller, who is responsible for returning it to the pool.

members.name: buffered-once
members.para: The values are read into a queue first, so the reader and its connection can be released before the result is consumed. Each value is removed as it is enumerated, so the result can be enumerated only once.

members.name: first-set
members.para: Only the first result set is read.

members.name: rowmap-once
members.para: Declare the once and pass it: a map built in the call (a new RowMap<T>(...) or a collection expression in the argument) is rebuilt, and its row reader compiled, on every call.
